topic: Portuguese and French in India — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The Portuguese explorer who reached the port of Calicut on India's Malabar coast on 20 May 1498 was:
questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama — landed at Kappad near Calicut on 20 May 1498, ending centuries-old Arab monopoly on the Indo-European spice trade route. Welcomed by Zamorin of Calicut. Made three voyages; died at Cochin (1524) on the third. Cabral followed in 1500 (also discovered Brazil en route). Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope (1488) but never reached India. Albuquerque was the second governor (1509-15) who captured Goa in 1510.

questions.stem: Goa was captured by the Portuguese in 1510 from:
questions.explanation: Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate (ruled by Yusuf Adil Shah) on 25 November 1510. Goa became the capital of Portuguese India. Notable Portuguese policy — 'Estado da Índia' (the State of India) ruled from Goa over Portuguese settlements stretching from East Africa to Macau. Goa Inquisition was established 1560 by Francis Xavier's request. Goa remained Portuguese until Operation Vijay liberated it on 19 December 1961, ending 451 years of Portuguese rule.

questions.stem: The French East India Company was established by Jean-Baptiste Colbert during the reign of Louis XIV in:
questions.explanation: Compagnie française des Indes orientales — founded 1664 by Colbert, Louis XIV's finance minister, much later than English (1600), Dutch (1602) or Danish (1616) companies. Headquarters at Surat (1668), then Pondicherry (1674). Other settlements — Chandernagore (1690), Mahe (1721), Yanam (1731), Karikal (1739). All five were transferred to India between 1949-54 (de jure 1962). The company was dissolved 1769 after losing the Carnatic wars.

questions.stem: The decisive Battle of Wandiwash (22 January 1760), which broke French power in India, was fought between:

options.option_text: Sir Eyre Coote (English) vs Comte de Lally (French)

questions.explanation: Battle of Wandiwash (Vandavasi, modern Tamil Nadu) — fought during the Third Carnatic War (1756-63) — Anglo-French rivalry. Sir Eyre Coote led the English; Comte de Lally the French. English victory was decisive; Pondicherry fell in 1761. Treaty of Paris (1763) restored Pondicherry to France but stripped it of military / political power — became merely a commercial outpost. Marks the 'end of French ambitions' in India. Robert Clive had earlier won Plassey 1757; Dupleix recalled to France 1754.

questions.stem: The Portuguese policy of 'Cartaz' was best described as:

options.option_text: A licence/pass system requiring all Asian ships to buy Portuguese permits to trade in Indian Ocean

questions.explanation: Cartaz (Portuguese for 'pass / placard') — Portuguese ships intercepted any Asian merchant vessel without one. Without a Cartaz, ships were considered hostile and could be sunk or seized. This monopolised the Indian Ocean trade — until the Dutch and English broke it in the 17th century. The system was the precursor to later European 'navicert' practices. Other Portuguese institutions in India — Estado da Índia (the colonial admin), the Goa Inquisition (religious court), Cidade Velha de Goa.

questions.stem: Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated from Portuguese rule by Indian armed action — codenamed 'Operation Vijay' — in:
questions.explanation: Operation Vijay (17-19 December 1961) — Indian forces under Maj Gen K.P. Candeth liberated Goa, Daman and Diu after years of failed diplomacy with Portugal under António Salazar. PM Nehru took the decision after the Portuguese refused all UN appeals. Casualties were minimal. Goa, Daman and Diu became a Union Territory in 1962. Goa attained statehood on 30 May 1987 (became 25th state). Daman & Diu merged with Dadra & Nagar Haveli in 2020 to form a single UT.

questions.stem: Joseph François Dupleix, the French Governor-General who built up French ambitions in South India in the 1740s, was based at:
questions.explanation: Joseph François Dupleix (Gov-Gen of French India 1742-54) operated from Pondicherry. He pioneered the use of European-trained Indian sepoys and the strategy of intervening in Indian princely politics — both later perfected by the British. He won the First Carnatic War (1746-48), but was overstretched in the Second (1748-54). Recalled to France in disgrace; died bankrupt 1763. The other 4 French settlements were smaller — Chandernagore (Bengal), Mahe (Malabar), Yanam (Andhra), Karikal (Tamil coast).
